title: mandate (SPEC 3.2 + 17.2): the principal's limits as code
description: SPEC 3.2 with the fields section 17 adds, all optional in the object and required by policy where a gateway wants them: expires_at (require.mandate_expiry), scope.counterparties (require.counterparty_allowlist), scope.purpose_codes (require.purpose_codes), scope.step_up_above_minor, scope.unattended (absent means false: a human must be present), principal_sig (require.principal_signature). Fields are only added (SPEC 8): verifyMandate keeps working on these objects and checks only what SPEC 3.2 defines; the gate enforces the rest. The free-text purpose stays for people and is never evaluated by a gate.

how.description: How the principal confirmed the limits. ap2_mandate: an AP2 payment mandate (SD-JWT) exists for it; the mandate here is AP2-shaped, not an AP2 credential.

counterparties.description: Sellers the agent may pay, in any form of _defs seller. ["*"] is the principal's explicit choice to allow any; an empty list is not allowed; absent: any, unless the policy requires an allowlist.

purpose_codes.description: The purpose as code, matched against the deal's purpose_code. No free text is ever evaluated.

step_up_above_minor.description: Above this amount every transfer needs a step_up object; null: never.

unattended.description: May the agent spend with no human present? Absent or false: every transfer is a step-up unless the gateway asserts human_present.

purpose.description: A sentence for people, no personal data. Never evaluated by a gate.

expires_at.description: Required by the reference policy (MANDATE_NO_EXPIRY). An ended mandate is a mandate_end statement, as in SPEC 3.2.

principal_sig.description: Optional: the principal's own Ed25519 signature over canonical(mandate without sig, principal_sig, pq_sig and pq_kid). The issuer's sig covers it. It proves that the holder of this key signed; that the key is the principal's is attested by principal_key in the agent identity, not by this field.
